message.reasoning_content:
We need to read the facts and determine which crimes are directly supported.

Facts: The defendant (佟某) used a knife to threaten victim (申某), forced him to give credit card password, then used the credit card to withdraw 2500 yuan. Also took 3000 loan? Actually Wu borrowed 3000 from victim, but not relevant. The defendant also took 1100 yuan cash found later. So crimes: robbery? Under Chinese law, robbery (抢劫) is using violence or threat to seize property. Here he used a knife to threaten and forced victim to give password and withdraw cash. That's robbery (using threat with a weapon). Also possibly "非法获取信用卡信息" but that's part of robbery. Could also be "诈骗"? No, he didn't deceive, he used force. Could be "非法持有、使用刀具"? Not a crime. Could be "敲诈勒索"? He threatened to get money, but it's robbery. Also "抢夺"? No, he used threat. So "抢劫罪". Also "非法占有他人财物" maybe "盗窃"? No, because used force. So only robbery.

But also "非法获取信用卡信息" maybe "侵犯公民个人信息罪"? He forced victim to give password, but that's part of robbery. Chinese criminal law: "抢劫罪" includes using threats with weapons to obtain property. So we list "抢劫". Also "非法持有、使用刀具" is not a separate crime. Could be "敲诈勒索罪"? That requires threat to disclose or harm unless victim pays. Here he threatened immediate violence, not extortion after. So robbery.

Thus answer: [罪名]抢劫<eoa>
